# Applicability of the nonregular same separator at selected logarithmic scales

This is a dependency audit with explicit realization bridges. In the established compact cardinality-minimal bad-base framework, let (C,L,epsilon) be a minimizing triple for beta_epsilon−tau log epsilon from `candidate 281b285239e28b38`. For all sufficiently small tau, the nonregular finite-contact response package **does apply** to the explicit cone of all continuous normal-dependent convex physical fields, together with the concave parameter directions described below, arbitrary cap-normal controls, and both logarithmic-scale directions.

The conclusion is a SAME separator for this specified physically realized cone. It is not an assertion that every formal signed boundary array is feasible, nor a derivative of a reoptimized parameter. Other-fiber supporting facets, nonsmooth bodies, and finite-PL parameter creases are allowed. There is no numerical Gamma payment.

## 1. Exact inputs and order of dependence

The following already proved inputs are used in this order.

1. The original compact positive-body/minor-quota framework and the quantitative joint value gap from `candidate 5dc06bb8226350eb`.
2. Actual scalar-penalized attainment and epsilon comparable to tau from `candidate 281b285239e28b38`, Sections 1–3. Their proof does not use a response separator.
3. Fixed-slice sampled polyhedrality and actual zero-plane cut exclusion. Thus take L=min_r A_r, strictly positive on C, with a positive extension to a neighborhood. Relevant sources are `candidate f17e4f2b0ba9ee84` and `candidate c3d41384eb67bd52`.
4. Uniform vanishing of the physical buffers and uniform own-source interiority/properness, from `candidate cebc39c4f5ccbc96` and Sections 1–3 of `candidate ed103e599726c87f`. These are geometric results, independent of a SAME separator.
5. Joint concavity, strict fixed-body concavity and the interior differential of the energy root, plus its full-supergradient extension on the canonical finite hull. These are in `candidate 5811f0ad1132ce56` and `candidate c0fc791108fc8765`.
6. The compact-tilt buffered balance and parity-face proof in `candidate 86dd5366456916a8` and `unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`. Section 2 below verifies their hypotheses for the FULL parameter L.
7. The signed energy envelope, exact contact-minimum continuation, and all-status cap inverse in `candidate d750a370b2e831ee`, `candidate c6bafe9ff5de0861`, and `candidate 8d34ae3d0117f855`.
8. Conservative inside-zero response and compact outside-selector duality in Section 7 of `candidate 4f875cf42fc6ba0a`, followed by the finite-contact bookkeeping in `candidate 1a7cfa3d1047cbae`.

Items 6–8 had explicit geometric or physical premises. Sections 2–6 below verify those premises here instead of citing the final conditional dual as an unconditional theorem.

Write N=d+1, dm for actual mixed volume, M=m(S), and Gamma(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u) for within-fiber covariance. All base statements are relative to aff(P). The buffer is

    f(z,x)=M^(−1/N) L(z,x)^(1/N) F(z,x)^(d/N),
    F(z,x)=E_(C_z)(x)^(1/d).                           (1)

At these selected minima epsilon tends to zero with tau. The geometric inputs give a uniform own-source ball and, for every deepest mark, a strict atomic gap and a proper shifted own section for every Gamma-normalized continuous normal. In particular **there are no atomic deepest rows** for sufficiently small tau. This fact is obtained before constructing the response dual.

## 2. Concavity, strict own concavity, and the prescribed supergradient

The positive weighted geometric mean G(l,F)=l^(1/N)F^(d/N) is concave and increasing in both variables. Consequently (1) is jointly concave on the canonical body, continuous there, positive on every real fiber interior, and zero on every fiber boundary. Here L is finite-PL and continuous, and the needed boundary continuity of F is an existing energy theorem, not an inference from concavity alone.

On a fixed own fiber, F is strictly concave between distinct interior marks. Its strict inequality and the strict increase of G in F imply strict concavity of f on that fiber's interior, even if L is nonsmooth there.

Every prescribed fiber supergradient g of f at an interior mark Y=(p,y) has a finite full extension. Indeed the ordinary fiber gradient of F is unique. The superdifferential chain rule for a positive smooth geometric mean gives

    g=f(Y) a_E + [f(Y)/(N L(Y))] c,                   (2)

where c is a fiber supergradient of L at Y and a_E is its ordinary energy normalizer. Since L is a finite minimum of affine planes, c is a convex combination of the continuous gradients of the planes active at Y. The same combination of their full gradients supplies a full supergradient (alpha_L,c) of L. The energy-root theorem supplies a full supergradient (alpha_F,grad_x F), including boundary bases. Then

    alpha=f(Y) alpha_L/[N L(Y)]
                  +d f(Y) alpha_F/[N F(Y)]           (3)

and g form a full supergradient of f. The global upper tangent inequality follows by first using the full upper tangents of L and F and then the concave tangent inequality for G. No assertion about an arbitrary concave function having finite boundary-base slopes is used.

## 3. Actual finite cover and finite contact sets

Fix the attained triple, its raw maximum Q and deepest bases I. Convexity of all right-quantile superlevel constraints shows I is lattice-complete: convex combinations of deepest marked points remain in the depth-Q region, and any integer base of such a combination belongs to P and hence I.

At every deepest Y=(p,y), the own-proper and atomic-gap hypotheses allow the archived finite clipping/minimum-norm reduction of base tilts. Near-active right Q-quantiles therefore lie in a compact parameter set and have positive own coarea. The concave source maximization argument supplies at most d+1 actual mass-Q caps, positive weights rho_j with sum one, and a fiber supergradient g such that

    Gamma(u_j)=1,  sum_j rho_j u_j=epsilon g,
    c_j=N_j.Y−epsilon f(Y).                          (4)

This construction does not require cap-mass differentiability at other fibers. Extend g by (3), and set a=sum rho_j a_j−epsilon alpha. The exact quantile inequalities at all deepest marks imply that a supports conv(I) at p. It vanishes on the minimal face F_p containing p.

For every z in F_p and every x in C_z, the old affine function

    P_i(z,x)=sum_j rho_j N_j.(z,x),  h_i=sum_j rho_j c_j

satisfies

    psi_i(z,x)=P_i(z,x)−h_i−epsilon f(z,x)>=0.         (5)

At every deepest mark with base z in F_p, all positively weighted Q-quantile inequalities are equalities, and hence psi_i=0.

There is exactly one such zero in each assigned sampled fiber. Two distinct interior zeros of (5) would contradict strict own concavity of f. An interior zero and a boundary zero would force zero along the intervening segment by convexity and nonnegativity of psi_i, again contradicting strict own concavity at two interior points. Since every assigned base is deepest, it has an interior zero. Thus the old contact set is finite and consists of one interior mark per assigned integer base. This argument does not need a differentiable L, a regular cap, or an affine graph between the contacts.

Choose one witness in each inclusion-maximal face among the F_p, p in I. These faces cover I. Witnesses in two different maximal faces cannot share parity: their integer midpoint belongs to I, and its minimal face contains both old faces. This contradicts maximality. There are therefore at most k(I)<=k(P) groups. For each selected group take J_i=I intersect F_i, a finite set; overlaps between groups are retained. The selected groups need not cover an entire affine fiber plane, and their continuous normals need not sum to zero.

## 4. One actual addable cone, with full normal dependence

Here is a direct realization of the archived normal-dependent convex potential cone. Let Phi(u,z,x) be continuous in all its arguments, with u on the unit continuous sphere, globally finite, and convex in (z,x) for each fixed u. It may have either sign. Define

    K_z(t)={x: u.x+t Phi(u,z,x)<=h_(K_z)(u)
                          for every unit u}.         (6)

For sufficiently small t>=0 these are positive compact convex bodies. Uniform convex lower linear bounds for Phi control large |x|, so all new bodies are bounded. On that common bounded set |Phi| is bounded by A. Hence K_z(t) subset K_z+t A Ball, while an inner homothety of K_z about an old inball center with factor 1−t A/r lies in K_z(t). These give positivity and O(t) radial displacement.

They are actually compatible. If q=sum lambda_j z_j and x_j in K_zj(t), convexity of Phi gives, for every unit u,

    u.(sum lambda_j x_j)+t Phi(u,q,sum lambda_j x_j)
       <=sum lambda_j [u.x_j+t Phi(u,z_j,x_j)]
       <=sum lambda_j h_(K_zj)(u)
       <=h_(K_q)(u).                                 (7)

Thus sum lambda_j x_j belongs to K_q(t). Their canonical hull has exactly these sampled fibers; lattice completeness preserves the same base P. Relative-rank hulls are treated in the inherited affine lattice, or by the already proved harmless rational perpendicular thickening if an ambient full-dimensional representative is required.

At a regular old boundary point x with unique unit normal n, the signed inward first speed of (6) is

    v_z(x)=Phi(n,z,x).                               (8)

To verify this without smoothness, write the new endpoint on the old ray from an interior origin. The old n-constraint bounds its relative radial displacement from below. A constraint active at the new endpoint has a convergent normal along a subsequence; its old slack tends to zero, so uniqueness of the old normal identifies that limit as n and gives the matching bound. The radial denominator is bounded away from zero by the old inball. Compactness and continuity give (8), and the uniform radial O(t) bound supplies dominated convergence. This is precisely the signed normal-roof argument already used in `candidate 2951c303a65db1e9`; it is not a new potential class.

Finite nonnegative sums of fields are still continuous convex fields and realize the SUM of their speeds by (8). Arbitrary signed normal-dependent affine fields are included, with both signs. In dimension one (6)–(8) are the two endpoint constraints and require no smoothness convention.

For parameters take every continuous h on a fixed neighborhood of C for which h+cL is concave there for some c>=0. On the same new bodies set

    L_t^raw=L+t h,
    L_t=L_t^raw exp[−M_t^(−1) integral_(S_t) log L_t^raw dm_t]. (9)

Since L has a positive neighborhood extension, these are positive and concave for all small t. Finite sums of these h are legal, using the sum of their constants c. The class includes both signs of affine functions, both L and −L, and negatives of all finite maxima of affine functions. The latter suffice for the finite-source volume-coupling separation. No closure of the radial parameter cone is required.

For every finite collection of fields and parameter directions, (6) and (9) realize their simultaneous nonnegative combinations on a common small interval. Add arbitrary finite cap-normal velocities and epsilon(t)=epsilon exp(s t), s in R. This is the concrete physically addable cone used below. It is not all conceivable signed speed arrays.

## 5. Uniform expansions and exact continuation for that cone

The radial hypotheses just proved imply the uniform signed energy expansion near every old contact mark. The energy minimizers stay in a compact set with a positive denominator floor on both old and new bodies. This is the full content of the archived uniform-energy-envelope theorem; no differentiable maximizing-mark path is needed.

The parameter expansion in (9) is also uniform near the contacts. Put

    D=integral_boundary v,
    s_L=M^(−1)integral_boundary log L v,
    H=M^(−1)integral_S h/L dm.

Since log L is Lipschitz on a common positive neighborhood, the signed shell formula gives

    L_t=L+t[h−L(H−s_L)]+o(t),
    f_t/f=1+(t/N)[h/L−H+s_L−C_E/E+D/M]+o(t).          (10)

The remainders are uniform on compact own-interior neighborhoods. There is no derivative of grad L across a crease. Within-fiber covariance has the usual exact first derivative (D Sigma−J)/M; all centroid derivative terms vanish against the old centered first moments.

For cap normals N_ij(t)=N_ij+t nu_ij, define A_i(t)=sum_j rho_ij Gamma_t(u_ij+t u'_ij) and the exact contact budget

    alpha_i(t)=min_(z in J_i,x in K_z(t))
       [sum_j rho_ij N_ij(t).(z,x)−h_i
                            −epsilon(t) A_i(t) f_t(z,x)].       (11)

All minimizers in (11) approach the finite zero set in (5). Boundary energy continuity excludes a remote boundary contact, and testing the old interior marks bounds the minimum above. The uniform expansion then gives exactly the minimum of the finitely many old-contact linear coefficients. In particular, with delta_ia=epsilon f(Y_ia), the coefficient at contact a is

    sum_j rho_ij nu_ij.Y_ia
      −delta_ia sum_j rho_ij grad Gamma(u_ij).u'_ij
      +delta_ia[C_E,ia/(N E_ia)+J_i/(2M)
          −(N+2)D/(2NM)−s_L/N−h(Y_ia)/(N L_ia)+H/N−s].         (12)

This agrees with the multicontact source, including every mass, covariance, parameter-normalization and scale term. The derivative at a new minimizing mark is not substituted for this finite minimum.

Each selected cap retains a proper own section, so its current tail has a continuous strictly decreasing local inverse near Q even if other traces are supporting. Solve the exact common-quantile equation

    sum_j rho_ij c_ij(t,q_i(t))=h_i+alpha_i(t).         (13)

By (11), at every point of every current assigned fiber at least one buffered threshold is at least its corresponding quantile in (13). Hence its buffered depth is at most q_i(t). Off the old finite deepest-base set, the strict compact gap persists by joint upper semicontinuity. Thus these are actual global covering comparisons along (6)–(9).

The cap directional response includes all supporting statuses. With proper coarea S_j>0 and proper-section first moment m_j, its exact response has inside positive hinges and outside negative hinges in the relative displacement r−nu_j.w. Drop the inside positive hinges but retain their full-fiber body term. This gives

    R_j^0(v,nu,r)=B_j(v)+S_j r−m_j.nu
       −integral_outside [(nu.w−r)/|u_j|−v(w)]_+ dS.            (14)

It is jointly concave, increasing onto the real line in r, and no larger than the exact loss. The all-status radial proof and bounded-plane-motion argument give the expansion uniformly for bounded r and nu; no C1 cap-mass premise remains. The exact threshold equalization from (13), combined with (14), yields a concave lower group loss, still taking the minimum over all contacts in (12).

## 6. One separator for the entire stated cone

If every group's conservative normalized improvement, including M tau s, were strictly positive for one member of the cone above, (11)–(14) and the off-base gaps would give an actual strict decrease of beta_epsilon−tau log epsilon. Attained minimality forbids this. The downward hypograph response cone is convex, and separation from the open positive orthant does not require its image to be closed.

For a finite collection of tests, each negative outside hinge is the infimum of its linear forms over densities 0<=theta<=1 on its actual old supporting face. Their body/coarea/moment images are compact. Proper coareas are positive; equalizing these forms produces the compact set of genuine conservative branch gradients. Separation gives one convex mixture over group, contact and selector indices.

For the entire test class choose the SAME dual by compactness before passing to any body limit. Its fixed finite-group variables are cap weights, contact weights, and bounded effective densities on the finitely many selected supporting faces. The coarea equations bound the contact weights, and each prescribed integrable speed or parameter test defines a weak-star closed condition. Every finite collection is feasible by the preceding argument; compactness gives their intersection. The same finite collection always includes arbitrary cap-normal coordinates and both signs of s. Consequently the resulting density Xi satisfies

    integral_boundary Xi_z(x) Phi(n_z(x),z,x) dS<=0            (15)

for **every** field in Section 4, with one common choice of all cap, contact and supporting allocations. Both signs of normal-dependent affine fields give the corresponding normal-localized full affine moment equalities. This is the archived normal-bundle cone from `candidate 7278f286325c46c7`, not a weaker position-only replacement.

The shared signed cap-normal variables give the allocated section mean at the kappa-weighted contact barycenter, with the weighted buffer shift. They do not give a separate section centroid at every individual contact. Parameter tests give the SAME-e full-space volume martingale and its PL contact/gradient labels, exactly as in the multicontact source. Those rows are not replaced by the unrelated parameter-only separator.

Finally the free signed scalar direction has common coefficient M tau−Delta. Therefore

    Delta=M tau.                                     (16)

There are no atomic rows in this small-tau application, and every own coarea is uniformly positive. Thus the geometric upper force bound and the row likelihood theorem can be combined with (16) without a remaining separator-applicability assumption for this explicit cone.

## 7. Affine nullity and precise limits of the conclusion

Common fiber-affine coordinate changes are actual symmetries of the invariant objective. They may be composed exactly with (6)–(9), pulling cap planes and the finite-PL parameter along the map. This retains affine nullity without claiming that −grad L.V is a uniform continuous parameter jet at moving creases. No such jet is inserted into the cone above. The response identities use exact composition when that symmetry is invoked.

This audit discharges the retained finite-cover, finite-contact, shape-envelope, supporting-cap and physically addable-cone premises at every sufficiently small selected logarithmic-scale minimum, **for the explicit normal-dependent convex-field/parameter class stated here**. It does not establish a dual simultaneously for every possible body deformation, every existential inside allocation, or a reoptimized-parameter derivative. Conservative inside-zero loss is sufficient for the necessary separator; exact inside response can be nonconcave.

The conclusion supplies the actual common certificate needed by the previously proved force and contact-parameter compactness bounds. It does not imply uniform integrability of inverse parameter densities at a moving zero boundary, identify original row means, or prove a sharp numerical depth bound.

The supporting-response and multicontact checkers were rerun during this dependency audit: `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_supporting_cap_directional_inverses_slab_recovery.py` passed **197 exact checks**, including 168 actual clipped parallelograms, and `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_nonregular_multicontact_log_flux_defect_transport.py` passed **813 exact aggregation and moment checks**. These verify the inherited algebra/calibrations, not the analytic applicability bridges proved above.
